title: Artificial neural networks identify prenatal exposure associations with maternal, placental and neonatal DNA methylation
summary: In an observational study of 28 mother–infant pairs, Auto-CM, a weighted associative artificial neural network, mapped associations between prenatal exposures and measured methylation across placental and maternal and neonatal buccal tissues. Reported links included maternal air-pollution exposure with MGMT methylation and prenatal stress with placental NR3C1 methylation. The small exploratory cohort supports associations only; it does not establish causal effects or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Auto-CM weighted associative artificial neural network

evidence.tested: Auto-CM was applied to measured questionnaire, exposure, and methylation data from 28 mother–infant pairs; the primary article reports tissue-specific associations.
evidence.unknown: The small observational study does not establish causality, independent replication, or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Auto-CM estimates weighted associations among prenatal exposures, clinical variables, and measured DNA methylation.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
